# 深密解脫經

**ID:** T0675
**Volume:** T16
**Category:** 經集部類
**Original Category:** 經集部
**Byline:** 元魏 菩提流支譯
**Dynasty:** 元魏
**Date:** 514
**Juans:** 5
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T0675

## Contributors
- 菩提流支 (A001357)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

T675 in five fascicles is the second-earliest complete Chinese rendering of the *Saṃdhinirmocana-sūtra* — the foundational sūtra of the Yogācāra school, expounding *ālayavijñāna* 阿賴耶識, the three self-natures (*trisvabhāva* 三自性), and the three dharma-cakra (三轉法輪) doctrine according to which the *Saṃdhinirmocana* itself is the third and definitive turning. The translation was carried out at Luòyáng 洛陽 by the North-Indian Yogācāra translator [Bodhiruci](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8F%A9%E6%8F%90%E6%B5%81%E6%94%AF) of Northern Wèi 北魏 in **Yánchāng 延昌 3 (514 CE)** under the Northern Wèi imperial translation programme.

**Abstract**

The Northern-Wèi recension is the second-oldest complete witness, preceded only by the partial *Buddhabhāṣita jiějié jīng* 佛說解節經 ([KR6i0355](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0355) / T677, single fascicle by [真諦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E8%AB%A6)/Paramārtha covering only the second chapter), and superseded by [Xuánzàng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98)'s definitive five-fascicle *Jiě shēnmì jīng* 解深密經 ([KR6i0353](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0353) / T676, dated 647). [菩提流支](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8F%A9%E6%8F%90%E6%B5%81%E6%94%AF) arrived in Luòyáng in 508 and worked under Wèi imperial patronage until the early 530s; the *Lìdài sānbǎo jì* 歷代三寶紀 ([KR6r0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0011), T2034) records the 514 date for this translation. The Tàishàngzhāo Tánníng 沙門都釋曇寧 preface preserved at the head of the *Taishō* witness — "夫至迹虛微、理包言像之外，幽宗沖祕、旨絕名相之域" ("The supreme trace is empty and subtle, its principle envelops what lies beyond word and image; the recondite tenet is deep and secret, its purport sunders the domain of name and mark") — frames the sūtra as the climactic turning of the wheel and the principal scriptural ground for *Yogācāra* teaching. The text is also the chief source for the four partial Chinese translations registered in the *Taishō* under T677–T679 (= [KR6i0355](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0355), [KR6i0356](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0356), [KR6i0357](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0357)).

The *Bodhiruci* version is structured in eleven chapters (品), one more than [Xuánzàng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98)'s ten-chapter version (the Wèi version splits Xuánzàng's first chapter "勝義諦相品" into two), and lacks the heavy *Yogācāra-vijñapti-mātra* terminology that [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) later standardized; for that reason it is an essential witness for both the Indian-language *vorlage* of the *Saṃdhinirmocana* and for the early-sixth-century pre-Xuánzàng Chinese Yogācāra vocabulary. *Saṃdhinirmocana* itself probably reached final form in northwest India between c. 200 and c. 350 CE.
